subject: Clarify buying lanes: marketplace vs direct contract
messages:
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@oasishealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Buying lanes question — marketplace vs direct contract

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the overview last week. We have an internal procurement review tomorrow and need a short briefing to decide whether to go through AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace listing (private offer) or pursue a direct contract with Redwood. High-level questions from legal and finance: 

- Can you summarize the invoicing flow and timing differences (marketplace invoice vs Redwood invoice)?
- Are there any differences in SOW/MSA terms that would block our security/compliance signoff?
- How do co-sell credits or channel rebates work if we list on marketplace vs direct sales?
- Any impact on PO handling, fiscal year timing, and vendor onboarding times?

I attached our RFP extract with the procurement checklist (oasis-rfp.pdf). A one-page comparison would be helpful. Can you send a short bulleted summary and the recommended path for a regulated healthcare deployment?

Appreciate it — we want to avoid surprises with our finance team.

Best,
Aisha
Procurement Manager | Oasis Health

[attachment: oasis-rfp.pdf]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@oasishealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-30T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buying lanes question — marketplace vs direct contract

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short primer and forwarded it to finance/security for any red flags. Key bullets below; I also attached a one-pager we use for account execs.

Summary (short):
- Marketplace (Private Offer via cloud marketplace):
  • Invoicing: typically through the cloud provider (monthly/quarterly) or via private-offer invoice flow — payment posts to provider then flows to Redwood; timing depends on provider settlement windows (can add 30–60 days).
  • Contracts: you can accept a private offer tied to your provider PO; however, for dev/prod SLAs and specific security terms (e.g., data residency, audit access), we recommend coupling with a Redwood amendment (we can push a short addendum).
  • Co-sell/credits: cloud partner co-sell credits can be available, but they are governed by the marketplace listing and channel registration. Marketplace listing may accelerate procurement approvals for teams used to buying from the provider.
  • Onboarding: vendor onboarding can be faster for teams that already have a marketplace vendor relationship; however, some procurement teams treat marketplace purchases as indirect and still require vendor forms.

- Direct contract (Redwood invoice / Private deployment):
  • Invoicing: direct invoices from Redwood; predictable net terms and the ability to set a specific billing cadence aligned to your FY.
  • Contracts: full MSA + SOW/Amendments under Redwood terms; easier to negotiate specific security items (SOC2, data access, on-prem options).
  • Co-sell/credits: less visible co-sell crediting via the cloud marketplace; partner incentives would be negotiated separately.
  • Onboarding: may take longer initially (vendor setup + PO vs private offer), but gives more control over custom terms.

Recommendation for Oasis Health (regulated healthcare):
- If you need strict contractual language for data residency, audit rights, and a short path to specific support SLAs, go direct with a Redwood contract and include the Redwood amendment.
- If procurement velocity and using existing cloud purchasing processes is the top priority (and provider settlement windows are acceptable), use a private offer on your cloud marketplace. We can attach an amendment for security items, but some legal teams push back on mixing third-party marketplace T&Cs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm preferred invoicing path (cloud invoice vs Redwood invoice).
2) If marketplace: I’ll open a private-offer template and loop our marketplace ops lead.
3) If direct: I’ll route our MSA + amendment and share expected negotiation timeline (usually 3–4 weeks).

Attached: redwood-buying-lanes-one-pager.pdf (quick comparison).

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with your procurement/legal today. What time works?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, East Region | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173

[attachment: redwood-buying-lanes-one-pager.pdf]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick playbook for Oasis Health — marketplace vs direct

Kimberly / Marcus — quick notes to support Kimberly's reply above before we engage procurement: 

- Marketplace private-offer play: best when customer needs faster PO/commit alignment and has existing marketplace procurement workflows. Trade-offs: settlement lag and sometimes limited ability to change provider-side terms.
- Direct play: better for customers requiring stronger contract controls (data residency, indemnities, audit windows). Also preferred when the customer requests on-prem or VPC/private deployments.
- Commercial levers to call out to procurement:
  • Billing cadence options (monthly/quarterly vs annual prepay)
  • Support tier (Standard vs Platinum) and response SLAs — include cost delta
  • Co-sell pathway: if they want partner-led deployment discounts, register opportunity with AWS/GCP/Azure to preserve credits (we should capture AWS opportunity ID).
- Timing expectations: market-private-offer setup = 3–10 business days to get private offer in place (depends on provider and whether a private offer template exists). Direct contract MSA + amendment = 10–20 business days (negotiation window).

Ask Marcus: can you prepare the private-offer template and a short clause we can include in a marketplace acceptance that covers: (1) data residency guarantee, (2) audit access for 12 months, (3) indemnity carve-out? I’ll include the ask on the procurement call.

Thanks — I’ll join the call if needed.
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@oasishealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-30T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buying lanes question — marketplace vs direct contract

Hi Aisha — quick follow-up after internal alignment. Below is a concise recommendation you can share with finance/legal ahead of your procurement meeting.

1) If your priority is procurement speed and you already use the provider marketplace: choose a Private Offer on your cloud marketplace.
   - Expect provider settlement windows that may push payment posting 30–60 days after invoice; confirm with your AP team if that timing is OK.
   - We will attach a short Redwood amendment for any security-specific items.
   - We will register the opportunity with the cloud partner (if you want co-sell crediting).

2) If you require bespoke contractual language (data residency, audit windows, custom SLA): pursue a direct Redwood contract.
   - We can align billing cadence to your FY and provide direct invoicing with agreed net terms.
   - Typical negotiation timeline: 2–4 weeks depending on redlines.

Attachments shared: redwood-buying-lanes-one-pager.pdf, redwood-private-offer-steps.docx. I also linked our private-offer template for legal review: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/docs/private-offer-template

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm which lane you prefer and whether AP can accept provider settlement timing.
- If marketplace: provide preferred cloud provider and I’ll kick off private-offer creation.
- If direct: I’ll route our MSA + amendment to your legal and share an initial draft within 48 hours.

Would 3pm PT today for a 20-min sync work? If not, share times and we’ll adapt.

Best,
Kimberly
Head of Sales, East Region | Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood-buying-lanes-one-pager.pdf, redwood-private-offer-steps.docx]
